notes: Single engine-assisted review of paired and separate Stockfish frames. References were saved before candidate output was read.

cases.rationale: Ng4 permits Bxg4, then the two played searches choose hxg4 and Qxg4 respectively. The better Rxc7 lines enter a forcing exchange rather than the same attack, so neither additional mechanism is isolated across the played searches.

fxe4 moves the f-pawn out of cover, and both played lines then show Bxg3 taking a second pawn near the king. c4 permits exf3 but retains the g-pawn through the early comparison. The played countercapture on f7 obscures a distinct material loss.

Both choices allow h6 and Ne8. Qb2 gives Black earlier queen activity, while f6 leaves a different defence, but the continuation does not isolate the queen activity or own king shelter as a cause of the loss.

After Qc7 both played searches start b4 and a more active queenside for White. Ne4 retains a central knight and the better lines follow a different plan. The later material and king-cover consequences differ between the played searches.

The two choices already lose heavily and both allow g4 and gxf3. The played lines differ later, and the independent deterioration is small. A choice-specific tactical or positional mechanism remains uncertain.
gxh5 is the leading supplied choice and the independent reply follows the same defence. No mistake verified.
Nxd5 and gxf5 have almost identical paired evaluations in a previously losing position. The independent replies vary, so the measured played comparison establishes no mistake.

cxd3 allows the same Rxd3 rook entry and moves White's c-pawn to d3. After c3 it remains on the c-file and both branches defend on the queenside differently. Later direct losses differ between the played lines.

Rcg1 allows Nxe4+ fxe4 Rf8+ Nf4 exf4 in both searches. The opening of the f-file in front of White's king has a separate structural consequence from the pawn and recapture sequence. The Ng3 lines move the king away from the f-file during the comparison.

The better Bc5 line also allows Bxf6 gxf6 Qg4+. The played lines rearrange the exchanges around d6 and permit similar g-file exposure. The shared check and pawn recapture cannot alone account for the choice-specific difference.
Rg8 and Rf7 tie within five centipawns in the paired search. The existing king pressure survives both. No additional mistake mechanism established.

Both exd5 lines permit Rxd5 and later Rxc3 and bxc3, displacing the b-pawn from the king's cover. Re1 keeps that cover in the early lines. The later material and checking effects differ between the played searches.
Re8 is the leading supplied choice. The later f-pawn and rook activity occurs in the corroborating search.
Qxf6 is the leading supplied choice and both searches corroborate the same queen exchange.
Rxe1 is the leading supplied choice. The f-pawn recapture occurs in both measured continuations.
Ne3 is close to a5 in both searches. Both choices retain a viable defence despite different pawn recaptures.
b4 is the leading supplied choice. Both searches retain queenside counterplay.
hxg5 is the leading supplied choice and both searches show the same knight recapture.
